newsitem.title: USA: U.S. PLAINS CATTLE ACTIVE AT $65, UP $1 - FEEDLOTS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. PLAINS CATTLE ACTIVE AT $65, UP $1 - FEEDLOTS.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle near midday Wednesday were trading actively at $65.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from light sales on Tuesday and late last week but steady with last week's top, feedlot sources said.
Over 20,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 40,000 sold in Kansas.
"It happened in one big whoosh," a Kansas feedlot operator said, "I wouldn't be surprised to see it all done by the afternoon and bids go back to $64.00," he said.
Packers reportedly had plenty of cattle to choose from and were being selective in their buying, sources said.
Showlists this week in Kansas were expanded by a large number of cattle carried over from last week, sources said.
Also, there were reports of packers buying cattle with extra delivery days attached, compared with normal seven-day deliveries, some sources said.
Fed cattle prices were supported by strong demand from packers looking to fill near-term inventory needs, said Dave Maher, analyst with Securities Corp. of Iowa.
"They knew if they bid $65.00, they could get all the cattle they needed," Maher said.
